newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Seven raw sugar cargoes in port - Russian official.
newsitem.headline: Seven raw sugar cargoes in port - Russian official.

text.p: Seven cargoes of raw sugar are waiting to dock at Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk, a port official said on Thursday.
The official said he believed the ships were of Cuban and Brazilian origin, but could not specify how much sugar was from each origin, or how many tonnes the cargoes represented altogether.
"Seven ships are waiting at roadstead, but not one of them is ready for offloading," the official said by telephone from the port.
"I believe there is Brazilian and Cuban sugar, but how much of each I can not say. I simply don't have the documentation to show me."
Novorossiisk officials in April reported a backlog of five cargoes of Cuban raws representing a total of 140,000 tonnes, indicating an average cargo size of 28,000 tonnes.
On the same basis the current backlog of seven cargoes would represent almost 200,000 tonnes of sugar.
The backlog of Cuban raws, caused by poor weather and rail transport limitations, has been clearing through April and May, port officials have said.
The official said on Thursday that one cargo of sugar had been forced to pay extra duties by the customs services, because the sugar it was carrying was at least partly refined.
"We have had a case where they started to offload a ship. However, the sugar was hardly raws, but 90 percent refined, and they were made to pay an extra duty," the official said.
Russia has slapped a 25 percent duty on all refined sugar imports, except those coming from Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, which have a customs treaty with Russia.
